source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Running usb port with CrystalDiskMark
1. Boot into OS.
2. Install USB 3.0 Type C test plug on an USB port.
3. Install the Benmark tool
4. Run BenchMark to USB Device

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: physical USB storage device + dd (operator plugs the device)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands:
# DUT: storage list + scratch write benchmark on an OPERATOR-DESIGNATED scratch path (never OS/system disk)
sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,MODEL 2>&1; dd if=/dev/zero of=${USB_BENCH_TMP:?operator must designate a SCRATCH file path, e.g. /mnt/<usb-mount>/scratch.bin - NEVER an OS/system disk} bs=1M count=1024 oflag=direct conv=fsync 2>&1; rm -f "${USB_BENCH_TMP:?}" 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return lsblk device list + the dd write throughput (MiB/s) so the operator compares with SPEC and the workstation CrystalDiskMark baseline.

historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED because the USB map, scratch path and numeric SPEC were absent; its safety analysis is retained but permanent BLOCKED conflicts with V3.1 readiness policy.

original_test_intent: Measure the approved USB device's bandwidth through the designated USB port using CrystalDiskMark and compare the raw benchmark results with the project-provided numeric specification.
original_method: An operator attaches the approved USB 3.0 Type-C benchmark device; the exact supported CrystalDiskMark profile runs only against owner-designated disposable test space, then raw results, device/link identity and unexpected logs are collected.
manual_activity: A qualified operator must attach the approved USB benchmark device and positively identify disposable test storage. Once that setup, the CrystalDiskMark profile and numeric criterion are approved, benchmark execution and evidence capture can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact SUT USB port/controller and approved Type-C benchmark device identity
Explicit disposable target volume/test file with sufficient free space and no protected data
CrystalDiskMark version, test size/count/profile and cache policy
Numeric bandwidth SPEC by metric with units and tolerance
Maintenance approval, data-retention/cleanup and I/O-error recovery plan
safety_requirements: Never target an OS, boot, mounted production, protected or ambiguously identified disk/volume.
Require positive device-to-volume mapping, free-space bounds and explicit authorization before any benchmark write.
Preserve existing logs and raw results; do not clear evidence or hide failures by rerunning.
Stop on target-identity drift, unexpected capacity use, I/O/filesystem/USB error, disconnect, thermal excursion or service impact.
agent_execution_scope: Inventory USB topology, device serial/link speed, volumes/mounts and target identity; validate the supplied SPEC and CrystalDiskMark profile.
After physical setup and approval, run the exact bounded benchmark once against only the authorized target and capture the complete result file/screenshot and timestamps.
Collect post-test filesystem/USB/platform health and compare each metric with the supplied threshold without issuing PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the device, port, disposable benchmark target, CrystalDiskMark profile and numeric SPEC.
Attach the physical device and confirm that no protected data or service depends on it.
Review raw metrics, coverage and health evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its lsblk inventory and explicit scratch-path guard are useful safety concepts, but dd write throughput is not CrystalDiskMark and does not reproduce its workload matrix, cache behavior or reported metrics. The nested quoting also risks expanding the target in the wrong shell.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the approved CrystalDiskMark executable/profile on the supported OS and selected disposable volume. Do not replace it with dd unless a project explicitly defines a separate non-equivalent plan and acceptance baseline.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: CrystalDiskMark, USB 3.0 Type-C device, SPEC comparison and 15/180-minute source fields are preserved; the 180-minute machine-time field is not silently converted into an unspecified benchmark loop.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind device serial, physical port/controller, link speed, authorized disposable target, CrystalDiskMark version/profile and metric-specific SPEC in a signed execution manifest; capture raw exports and health telemetry.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only an OS and USB device supported by the approved CrystalDiskMark/project method.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record the exact CrystalDiskMark build, OS/driver and USB bridge/device firmware.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use the approved CrystalDiskMark documentation and project device/SPEC documentation supplied for execution.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target identity, workload reproducibility, safety bounds and numeric acceptance without changing the benchmark family.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; all configured metrics must be compared separately and reported with units/tolerances.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Device/volume map, profile and numeric SPEC.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Benchmark results depend on test size, queue/thread settings, cache, filesystem, bridge and thermal state; cross-tool figures are not directly interchangeable.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve another target, profile, duration or tool only with its own equivalence/acceptance evidence. Completing that approved plan must not be represented as the original CrystalDiskMark profile or unspecified master SPEC.
expected_evidence: SUT, port/controller, USB device serial/link and authorized target-volume mapping
CrystalDiskMark version and full test profile, numeric SPEC/tolerances and approval
Complete raw benchmark results for each metric with timestamps and comparison table
Pre/post filesystem, capacity, USB/kernel/system/BMC health, cleanup proof, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The procedure names CrystalDiskMark and the criterion requires SPEC comparison. The absent numeric thresholds and workload settings are project readiness inputs, not contradictory source statements.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The benchmark intent, target class and acceptance relationship are understandable. V3.1 explicitly treats missing SPEC, tool profile and project target as readiness gates; physical setup followed by an automatable benchmark is PARTIAL, not permanent BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains its target-safety concept but rejects dd as an unproven substitute for CrystalDiskMark.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains all listed missing inputs and write safeguards but reclassifies BLOCKED to PARTIAL under the locked V3.1 project-readiness rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates artifact readiness, physical setup, automatable core execution, Tool Result and engineer-owned verdict.

review_improvement: Prevents writes to the wrong disk and avoids a false equivalence between dd and CrystalDiskMark while keeping the case executable when project inputs arrive.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source has a clear benchmark purpose and named method; missing thresholds do not make its semantics unknowable. Physical device attachment makes the case PARTIAL, and the write benchmark is permitted only after exact target authorization and can then be automated.
